title: Dichotomy of control
idea: Some things are up to you: your judgments, choices, and effort. Everything else is not, including outcomes and other people.
apply: When something worries you, split it into two lists. Act on the first and let go of the second.
remind: Do your part. Release the outcome.
who: Leo, a salesperson waiting on a client's decision.

scenes.nar: Leo has a big pitch on Friday. His mind is full of things: the client's decision, the budget, his demo, and his follow-up.
He loses sleep over whether they will say yes and whether budgets get cut. Those are not his to decide, so the worry changes nothing.
So he sorts them into two lists. The decision and the budget are not up to him. His preparation, his follow-up, and his conduct are.
He puts his energy into the second list. He rehearses twice, sends a thoughtful follow-up, and sleeps well. Whatever they decide, he did his part.
